ch5_lab_boilerplate.title: Quick Check: The HTML Boilerplate & Doctype

questions.q: What is the correct HTML5 doctype declaration?
options: <!DOCTYPE HTML PUBLIC "-//W3C//DTD HTML 4.01//EN">
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html5>
<!TYPE doctype="html5">

questions.q: How did XHTML's rules differ from HTML5's, according to the chapter?
options: XHTML required every tag closed and lowercase with no exceptions; HTML5 relaxed those strict rules
XHTML and HTML5 have identical rules
HTML5 is stricter than XHTML about closing tags
XHTML came after HTML5

questions.q: Which part of the HTML boilerplate is described as "the brain of the page," holding info the user doesn't see (like the title and meta tags)?
options: <html>
<head>
<body>
<footer>

ch5_lab_semantics.title: Quick Check: Semantic Tags & Grouping Elements

questions.q: Why does the chapter say you should sell 'Semantic Architecture' using tags like <article> and <nav> instead of generic <div> tags?
options: Semantic tags load faster in every browser
They explicitly tell Google and screen readers what the content means, which boosts SEO and accessibility
Div tags are being removed from HTML6
There's no real difference, it's just a style preference

questions.q: What is the key difference in behavior between a <div> and a <span>?
options: <div> is a block element that takes the full width and starts a new line; <span> is inline and only takes the space its content needs
<span> always starts a new line; <div> never does
They behave identically in every browser
<div> is only for images; <span> is only for text

questions.q:
Following the "First-In, Last-Out" nesting rule, if you open

and then inside it, which tag must you close first?
options: , because it was opened first
<em>, because it was opened last
It doesn't matter which one closes first
Both must close on the same line

questions.q: Why must every <input> have a matching <label> linked by for/id?
options: It's optional styling that makes the form look nicer
A screen reader can't tell a user what a blank text field is for without it -- it's a required accessibility link
Labels are required for the form to submit data at all
Only <textarea> elements need labels, not <input>

questions.q: What does wrapping form fields in <fieldset> with a <legend> do for a screen reader user?
options: It hides those fields from screen readers entirely
It announces the group's name (like "Personal Information") before reading the fields inside it, giving context
It automatically validates the fields
It changes the fields' HTML input type

questions.q: A "Skip to main content" link helps a keyboard-only user, but a mouse user never notices it exists. Why?
options: It only works on mobile devices
A keyboard user would otherwise have to Tab through the entire nav menu every page load just to reach the content; a mouse user just clicks directly where they want to go
It's a decorative element with no real function
Mouse users can't see hidden links at all
